task: Find all molecules mentioned in PubMed for which oral bioavailability status has been reported.
task_instantiation:
Extract reports of **oral bioavailability** for molecules/compounds (and, if present, compound classes) in the provided PubMed paper text.

Create one record **each time a passage reports an oral bioavailability result for a specific molecule under a distinct context**. A distinct context is a change in any of: species/population (e.g., rat vs human; healthy volunteers vs patients), disease state (e.g., cirrhosis), metabolizer phenotype/genotype (e.g., poor vs extensive metabolizers), dose level, formulation/dosage form/salt/prodrug, or oral exposure mode (e.g., tablet vs capsule; solution; dietary exposure vs gavage). If the passage gives multiple doses/contexts for the same molecule, emit separate records.

In-scope evidence (must be explicit):
- Explicit oral bioavailability/systemic availability/absolute bioavailability/"F" after oral (PO) administration, including numeric values (%, fraction), ranges, mean±SD/CI, or qualitative descriptors (e.g., "low", "unpredictable", "almost complete").
- Statements where oral bioavailability is **calculated/derived** by comparing oral vs IV dosing (still in-scope; capture as oral bioavailability).
- Comparative oral-bioavailability claims (e.g., "3-fold higher with dietary route vs gavage", "lower than parenteral", "similar to rectal") **only if explicitly framed as bioavailability/systemic availability**.

Out of scope (do NOT extract):
- Permeability/BCS class, absorption-only statements that do not explicitly state/label bioavailability (unless the authors explicitly equate them, e.g., "bioavailability indicates complete absorption").
- Bioavailability for non-oral routes (IV, rectal, buccal, intranasal, etc.) except when used as a comparator to compute/describe oral bioavailability.
- Purely methodological formulas without a reported oral bioavailability outcome/value (unless the passage also provides the value elsewhere in the same passage).

Field filling rules:
- Use `molecule_name` as written.
- Put the reported oral bioavailability result in `oral_bioavailability_value` exactly as stated (keep %, ranges, ±, CI). If only qualitative/comparative information is given, store that phrase as the value.
- Set `bioavailability_report_type` based on wording (absolute vs systemic availability vs extent F, etc.). If unclear, use `unspecified`.
- Put species or human subject description in `species_or_population` (e.g., "pigs", "healthy postmenopausal women", "patients with cirrhosis").
- Put the oral dose (and units) in `dose` if stated.
- Put truly qualifying/non-standard conditions in `qualifying_conditions` (e.g., cirrhosis, poor metabolizers, sustained-release form, salt form), otherwise null.
- Use `extra_details` for comparators (IV/rectal/parenteral), calculation notes (AUC ratio), sample size, min/max, and any nuance not captured elsewhere.

schema_spec.name: molecule_name
schema_spec.description: Name of the molecule/compound (or compound class) for which oral bioavailability is reported in the passage.

schema_spec.name: oral_bioavailability_value
schema_spec.description: The reported oral bioavailability/systemic availability result for this molecule under oral administration, as stated (e.g., "41%", "10–22%", "0.61 ± 0.16", "low", "unpredictable", "3-fold higher vs gavage"). Null if the passage does not actually report an oral bioavailability outcome.

schema_spec.name: bioavailability_report_type
schema_spec.description: How the paper describes the oral bioavailability measure.

schema_spec.name: species_or_population
schema_spec.description: Species and/or human population for the oral bioavailability result (e.g., "rat", "pigs", "healthy postmenopausal women", "patients").

schema_spec.name: dose
schema_spec.description: Oral dose and units associated with the reported bioavailability (e.g., "50 mg", "100 µg/kg", "400 mg/m²").

schema_spec.name: oral_exposure_mode
schema_spec.description: How the oral dose was given if specified (e.g., "tablet", "capsule", "nasogastric gavage", "dietary pellets", "sustained release").

schema_spec.name: qualifying_conditions
schema_spec.description: Non-default or special conditions that materially qualify the oral bioavailability claim (e.g., "cirrhosis", "poor metabolizers", "administered as lysine salt", "first-pass metabolism noted"). Null if standard/unspecified.

schema_spec.name: comparator
schema_spec.description: Comparator route/dosing used to compute or contextualize oral bioavailability if explicitly stated (e.g., "vs IV", "vs parenteral", "vs rectal", "dietary vs gavage").

schema_spec.name: extra_details
schema_spec.description: Free-form string for additional details that do not fit other top-level fields.
